content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Draw and label tree diagrams for two or more successive events
Apply the AND rule (multiply along branches) for combined events
Apply the OR rule (add between outcomes) for alternative events
Calculate probabilities for independent events using tree diagrams
Solve problems involving coins, dice, spinners, and other contexts

In a quiz, the probability of getting question 1 right is $0.8$, question 2 right is $0.6$, and question 3 right is $0.5$. The questions are independent. Find the probability of getting all three right, and the probability of getting exactly two right.
$P(\text{exactly 2 tails}) = \frac{3}{8}$ (paths: HTT, THT, TTH each with probability $\frac{1}{8}$).

$P(\text{all right}) = 0.8 \times 0.6 \times 0.5 = 0.24$. $P(\text{exactly 2}) = (0.8 \times 0.6 \times 0.5) + (0.8 \times 0.4 \times 0.5) + (0.2 \times 0.6 \times 0.5)$. Wait — exactly 2 right means one wrong. Paths: right-right-wrong $(0.8 \times 0.6 \times 0.5 = 0.24)$, right-wrong-right $(0.8 \times 0.4 \times 0.5 = 0.16)$, wrong-right-right $(0.2 \times 0.6 \times 0.5 = 0.06)$. Total $= 0.24 + 0.16 + 0.06 = 0.46$.
